key_insight: A bi-polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial carbon-negative agent sharply boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a scalable route to improve photocatalytic carbon conversion by coupling catalyst design for CO2 activation with a renewable biological feedstock that also captures CO2.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite and pyrochlore phases.
Used Cs/Ba to raise surface basicity for CO2 chemisorption, Bi lone pairs for polarization, and Nb/Ta octahedra for charge transport.
Compared photocatalytic CO2 conversion under three conditions: no sacrificial agent, microplastics, and microalgae.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by about 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical deployment may depend on controlling microalgae handling, reactor compatibility, and whether biomass supply and separation remain efficient at scale.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
